memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make two gold rings and attach them to the other two corners of the breastpiece on the inside edge next to the ephod. Make two more gold rings and attach them to the bottom of the shoulder pieces on the front of the ephod, close to the seam just above the waistband of the ephod. The rings of the breastpiece are to be tied to the rings of the ephod with blue cord, connecting it to the waistband, so that the breastpiece will not swing out from the ephod." - Exodus 28:26-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God adds still more fastenings, and finally states the reason plainly: "so that the breastpiece will not swing out from the ephod." He wanted it held close against the priest's body, not flapping loose as he moved. The names of His people were to stay pressed near, not drift away at a distance.

That small purpose statement is tender. God cared about closeness. It was not enough for the names to be attached; they had to be held near. The design was intended to keep His people close to the heart of the one who represented them.

This is how God holds you. Not at arm's length, not loosely attached, but close. Isaiah pictures God gathering the lambs in His arms and carrying them close to His heart (Isa 40:11). And Jesus, our Great High Priest, does not represent us from a distance — He took on our flesh, knows our weaknesses, and sympathises with us (Heb 4:15). If you have been feeling far from God, remember the blue cords. His design has always been to keep you near.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I picture God holding me close, or keeping me at a distance?
What is making me feel far from God, and can I bring it to Him honestly?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You do not hold me loosely but keep me close to Your heart. When I feel distant, draw me near again and remind me that Your design has always been closeness. Amen.
